result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A opens by saying plainly that the setup is sound and explains why, covering every strength. It makes one explained fix (650 to 600/700) and presents the other ideas as optional. B also changes only small things, but it rewrites the whole file and adds several changes nobody asked for (text-wrap, th.num, pre, h3 letter-spacing). It also gets one detail wrong: unlike CSS weights 600 or 700, 650 has no single fallback weight, so browsers don't round it in one consistent way. B's changes still get short explanations. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B says plainly at the start that the setup is sound and explains why point by point. It makes just one small, explained fix (the 650 weight) and labels everything else as optional. A also opens by affirming the setup and explains each change, but it adds several changes that weren't requested (text-wrap, th.num, pre rules, letter-spacing split) and rewrites the whole file, which goes against the restraint the rubric asks for.
